bindings.explanation: Money PHP carries source currency and tracks residual units so successful allocation can conserve the total. It chooses recipients by fractional loss, whereas Core uses declared order; conservation does not settle that policy choice.
bindings.limits: Allocation path only. Amount and currency are retained, but largest-fraction recipient selection differs from Core declared-order distribution. BCMath intermediates and float ranking were not executed or exhaustively verified.

bindings.explanation: The inspected allocation guards and local result construction do not assign to the source Money amount or currency when rejecting invalid ratios. This supports operand preservation in that path, not every observable financial effect in the whole library.

bindings.explanation: With FloorToFirst, positive integer weights and an explicitly matched fixed unit context, Brick allocates the source magnitude, assigns remaining steps in order and restores the sign. The selected negative cases exercise the same signed allocation approach.
bindings.limits: FloorToFirst strategy, positive integer weights and a fixed context with explicitly matched scale/step. Other strategies, rational/zero-weight inputs and Brick Math internals are not claimed equivalent to Core.

records.claim: Brick Money — Ordered allocation in explicit integer steps

bindings.explanation: RubyMoney carries the remaining amount through successive splits, with selected tests checking the final sum. This numeric helper does not establish currency preservation, and its algorithm/input domain differs from Core allocation.
bindings.limits: A numeric helper, not a complete Money operation: currency construction is outside the reading. Successive division, numeric types and decimal cutoff affect the result; all-zero weights are replaced with equal weights.

records.claim: RubyMoney — Allocation carries residual value through successive splits

bindings.explanation: The inspected addition path checks currency compatibility before combining amounts and rejects a mismatch with both currencies identified. This supports the addition control; other comparisons and conversions were not reviewed.
bindings.limits: The inspected Money/BigMoney addition path checks currencies. Full ordering, equality, conversion and provider semantics were not assessed. Native exceptions are not portable FinKore error codes.

records.claim: Joda-Money — Money addition checks currency before combining amounts

bindings.explanation: Dinero separates its calculator from money operations. The inspected number path has precision limits and a no-progress guard; choosing a monetary library or calculator does not by itself establish exact arithmetic.
bindings.limits: The safe API and selected number-backend utility were read. Remainder goes to larger weights; zero ratios and scale derivation differ from Core. The no-progress guard is not proof of exact conservation beyond safe number precision.

bindings.explanation: The inspected Dinero distribution utility gives residual units to larger weights. For 801 units and weights [1, 3], its test expects [200, 601]; Core declared-order allocation gives [201, 600]. Both preserve the total at these small values.
bindings.limits: The safe API and selected number-backend utility were read. Remainder goes to larger weights; zero ratios and scale derivation differ from Core. The no-progress guard is not proof of exact conservation beyond safe number precision.

records.claim: Dinero.js — Allocation prioritizes larger weights for residual units

bindings.explanation: GoMoney equal splitting distributes signed residual units to the first positions. Its ratio method also accepts all-zero weights and can return zeros for a nonzero source, so the broader method is not a conservation guarantee.
bindings.limits: Signed equal splitting and ratio allocation were read. Equal splitting preserves signed residuals in the selected cases; an all-zero ratio list can return zero amounts for a nonzero source. Fixed-width overflow limits remain unverified.

records.claim: GoMoney — Signed splitting preserves residual units, except the zero-weight fallback

bindings.explanation: NodaMoney rounds during construction using the selected or ambient context; the standard path can choose currency scale. This contrasts with a generic exact-value boundary and shows why a composing rounding policy must be expressly identified.
bindings.limits: Constructor and rounding/context paths only. A missing context can select an ambient policy; standard rounding normally derives scale from currency. An expressly declared composing-domain policy is a separate assessment.

bindings.explanation: An omitted NodaMoney context can resolve to a global or thread-local policy and affect the constructed amount. Reproducing the outcome therefore requires identifying the applicable context; ambient lookup alone is not a portable context contract.
bindings.limits: Constructor and rounding/context paths only. A missing context can select an ambient policy; standard rounding normally derives scale from currency. An expressly declared composing-domain policy is a separate assessment.

records.claim: NodaMoney — Context-selected rounding can change a value at construction

bindings.explanation: py-moneyed rejects mismatched-currency addition and retains currency in new results. Its native equality returns false for different currencies, so the finding is a partial match rather than evidence for every operation in this rule.
bindings.limits: Addition/subtraction and selected equality/context observations only. Decimal representation alone does not establish unrestricted exactness; native numeric-zero conveniences and equality semantics differ from the portable boundary.

bindings.explanation: The selected py-moneyed rounding test changes its expected result when the active Decimal rounding context changes. This identifies a material numeric dependency, while the full arithmetic context remains unverified.
bindings.limits: Addition/subtraction and selected equality/context observations only. Decimal representation alone does not establish unrestricted exactness; native numeric-zero conveniences and equality semantics differ from the portable boundary.

records.claim: py-moneyed — Addition is currency-checked, but numeric context remains observable

bindings.explanation: Beancount balance checks use explicit tolerance or derive it from decimal precision and an option. Those facts change assertion outcomes and must be retained for reproduction; ledger tolerance remains separate from exact Money equality.

bindings.explanation: Moov recomputes file-to-batch and batch-to-entry totals rather than relying on structural acceptance. This payment-domain control illustrates evaluating related values together; it is not an implementation of the bounded Core Entity model.
bindings.limits: ACH file/batch control validation, not current Core payment semantics or a certification against a Nacha edition. Selected totals checks and assertions do not prove all variants, bounds or settlement behavior.

bindings.explanation: Formance constructs inverse postings in another transaction value. The helper alone establishes neither a verifiable original-event link nor a persisted reversal, making it a useful boundary example for this rule rather than a demonstrated match.
bindings.limits: Constructing inverse postings is not persisted reversal. Original-event linkage, one-time eligibility, authorization and committed history were not established. Amount pointers are shallow-copied, so deep ownership is not proven.

records.claim: Formance Ledger — Reversal swaps posting direction and reverses posting order
